text:
michael: seeing a sustained p99 spike (~450ms -> 1.8s) out of MIA POP starting ~00:07 UTC, throughput down ~25% on gen-4-small instances. graphs: https://grafana/rd/miapop
anya: any recent deploys to that POP? :eyes:
michael: no app deploys. there was a kernel selector tweak rolled last night (selector-v2) but only in eu/us-east. MIA got the binary via rolling image sync at 23:50 UTC
devon: I'm seeing a lot of TCP RTOs and retransmits from provider ASN 61234 on the POP egress. tcpdump snippet:
```
14:03:12.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 10.1.2.45.52344: R  seq 0 ack 0 win 0
14:03:12.223567 IP 10.0.5.12 > 10.1.2.45: retransmission
```
michael: also kvcache stats spiking: hot_evictions++ and kv_lock_wait median up 6x. profile attached: schedule_batch timeouts and kv_lock_wait shows long tail
infra-bot: [alert] mia-pop: network packet drop > 3% for ASN 61234 for last 10m
james: could be path flapping causing bursts of packet loss -> TCP backoff -> client RTTs inflate -> our batcher sees long tails -> kernel falls back to conservative single-thread kernels
anya: do we have kernel-selector logs? which kernel got picked during the tail?
michael: yes. snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T00:06:58Z] kernel_selector: picked generic_attention_slow for model: redwood-lite@v2 (fallback)
[2026-03-18T00:07:05Z] kernel_selector: fallback_reason=high_packet_retransmits
```
devon: that fallback path bypasses our async batching in a few places and takes the kv cache lock in-line. when network stalls, requests pile up and hit the hot key path -> kv_lock_wait climbs
sre_elena: can we mitigate by routing the MIA egress through our secondary provider (ASN 63500)? what's the roll plan?
james: quick mitigation: 1) BGP temp announce to route sensitive subnets via partner 63500 (5 min change), 2) increase kvcache lock shard count to reduce contention (hotfix config), 3) revert kernel-selector fallback to keep preferred kernels while we assess
michael: rolling BGP change now (in progress) and increasing kv shard config on canaries
anya: also throttling batch size for MIA service-route by 20% to reduce head-of-line blocking
infra-bot: [change] bgp-route-update initiated by james at 1966501310
devon: after the route flip p99 dropped to ~380ms, retransmits down. kv_lock_wait tail reduced but still elevated on a small set of hosts
michael: opening incident page: https://incidents/RED-2026-0318-mia-path (assigning to devon + sre_elena). will collect tcpdumps, perf profiles, and kernel-selector traces for the affected hosts
sre_elena: if provider confirms intermittent peering, we'll plan a more permanent egress preference and ask networking to set up automated failover. also want postmortem: root cause (provider flapping) + why kernel-selector reacted to network signals so strongly
anya: ack. i'll capture the batcher trace sets and run local repro with induced packet loss to confirm the path
james: next steps: keep route via 63500 until midnight UTC, push kv shard hotfix, increase batch timeouts in MIA for safe backpressure. will update thread.
michael: thanks team. short-term metrics look better; keeping monitoring on high-alert. :thumbsup:
